summary: Ulcer Index: the root-mean-square of percent drawdowns from the 14-bar high, with a stress level at 5.
overview: The Ulcer Index measures downside risk in its own pane. It rises when price falls from recent highs and stays down, and it stays near zero in steady uptrends.
A dashed stress line sits at 5 by default, and the line shifts to red as it nears that level. Drawdown columns can be shown too.
how: At each bar, percent drawdown = (close - highest close of 14 bars) / highest close x 100. Square these values, average them over 14 bars and take the square root.
Deeper and longer drops raise the index more than short, shallow ones.
use: Use it to see how painful recent declines have been.
Some traders compare the index across symbols to judge downside risk.
Watch readings above the stress line as deep or long drawdowns.
Use it with trend tools to see if a pullback is getting larger.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It only looks at drops from highs, not upside moves.
